prompt: If I randomly select i.i.d. samples from a distribution n times, the distribution of the sampled variables will approximately follow a normal distribution as n becomes very large. This statement is based on which theory?
answer:
This is based on the **Central Limit Theorem (CLT)**—with an important correction.

The CLT says that if \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) are i.i.d. observations with finite mean \(\mu\) and variance \(\sigma^2\), then the **sample mean**

\[
\bar X_n=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n X_i
\]

is approximately normally distributed for large \(n\):

\[
\bar X_n \approx N\left(\mu,\frac{\sigma^2}{n}\right).
\]

Equivalently,

\[
\frac{\sqrt n(\bar X_n-\mu)}{\sigma}
\Rightarrow N(0,1).
\]

The individual sampled variables do **not** become normally distributed; they retain the original population distribution. It is the distribution of **sample means across many repeated samples** that becomes approximately normal.
